newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 16.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Wednesday:
- Haughey off the hook with questions unanswered in payments to politicians tribunal
- Gay serial killer hunted in fashion guru Gianni Versace murder.
- Irish pound gets dollar aid as sterling surge eases
- Stentor lost 1.57 million punts as it plans autumn DCM float
- Intel earnings slip on European weakness
- Irish financier Dermot Desmond raises his stake in Unidare to almost 19 percent
- Aer Lingus new 2.0 million punt dedicated check-in facility at Dublin Airport.
- UBS suggests U.S. merger for JS Corp in bid to build on market presence
- Opposition calls on prime minister Bertie Ahern to investigate Haughey
- Catholic women shot dead at protestant boyfriend's home
- Dr Mo Mowlam was under pressure to make a Commons statement over continuing contact between British goverment officials and Sinn Fein
- Pressure eased on the punt but it remains near the top of the ERM band
- The Irish government will make tax cuts in its November budget, but spending is likely to be tightly controlled - The jobs of 160 workers at the Farah clothing company in Co Mayo have been saved
- Haughey received money from fraudster Patrick Gallagher - Revenue bonanza may see 600 million punt budget giveaway for taxpayers
